name: Alec Carruthers
description: Alec Carruthers is an MIT EECS PhD student studying data-efficient learning and foundation models for biological science.
photoAlt: Alec Carruthers seated outdoors beneath trees
bio: I’m a first-year PhD student in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at MIT. I’m interested in how data shapes what models learn: how dataset curation affects generalization, how to learn efficiently from limited data, and how to keep learning as data changes.

Previously, I was an AI Research Engineer at MIT Lincoln Laboratory, working on biomedical foundation models, multimodal learning, and ultrasound diffusion models. Before that, I worked on hyperspectral imaging and self-supervised learning at Apeel Sciences.
My research interests also include diffusion and flow models for molecular design and discovery, and foundation models for biological science.

education.note: Thesis on the GeoFlood flood-inundation mapping framework

teaching: At UT Austin, I was a teaching assistant for Linear Algebra and Differential Equations from June 2019 to December 2020.
